narrative.intro: Regents of the University of California has $162M in federal contract obligations for FY2027 to date. Regents of the University of California received 1 award so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $162M. Obligations are down 87.7% year over year. Historical obligations show large swings: FY22 was $6.7M, FY23 was $982M, FY24 was $1.4B, FY25 was $1.3B, FY26 was $1.3B, and FY27 is $162M to date. The current-year totals are partial because the period is fiscal year to date, and the note clarifies that the figures are contract obligations except where award-value figures are specified. This profile highlights a single large award in the current fiscal year and substantial variability in annual obligations over the last six fiscal years. Contractors and agency buyers tracking Regents of the University of California should note the single-award pattern for FY2027 to date and the marked year-over-year decline in obligations.

Prior fiscal years include larger totals such as $1.4B in FY24 and $1.3B in FY25 and FY26, which make the current-year total appear much smaller. sections.heading: How have obligations trended across recent fiscal years?
sections.body: Regents of the University of California obligations rose from $6.7M in FY22 to $982M in FY23, then peaked at $1.4B in FY24 before holding at $1.3B in FY25 and FY26. FY27 is $162M to date. The year-over-year change for the current fiscal year is down 87.7% compared with the prior year.
